title: Fake crypto app on Apple App Store linked to $23K wallet theft
content_md: A fake cryptocurrency trading app called Padre Terminal, previously available on the Apple App Store for iOS devices, has been linked to the theft of approximately $23,000 from 27 Solana wallets. Blockchain investigator Iris confirmed that one victim was compromised through the malicious App Store app, but has not determined how the other affected wallets were compromised. The researcher says the app drains wallets after unsuspecting users import their private keys into it. Padre was a cryptocurrency trading platform, mainly used to buy and sell meme coins on Solana. It was later renamed Terminal by pump.fun, a platform focused on creating, buying, and selling cryptocurrency “meme coins” on the Solana blockchain. Iris says the legitimate Padre trading service, now Terminal by pump.fun, is web-only, so any mobile apps impersonating it, including the one previously available on the App Store, are malicious. At the time of BleepingComputer's initial investigation, we found two Padre apps on the App Store (ID 6802739263 and ID 6717572591). The former was the Iris-confirmed drainer app, while the latter is likely pump.fun's official app, live since October 2024. The malicious Padre Terminal app has since been removed from the App Store, with its listing now returning a 404 error. Iris told BleepingComputer it suspects the trading interface of the fake app is served remotely, but has not directly observed the wallet-draining screen.
